description:
Found and fixed alongside fz-5xp.38 and fz-5xp.46.

    fnp classify(x :: float) when -x > 0.0, do: :negative_float
    fnp classify(_), do: :other
    fnp pick(0), do: -4.5
    fnp pick(_), do: -9

    classify(pick(0))    interp :negative_float    run/build ABORT in fz_unbox_int

The operand's type is a union at the call, and although the `x :: float` head
gates the clause, the plan had not narrowed it by the time the GUARD lowered.
`lower_neg` could prove neither lane and fell to `as_raw_i64`.

It was specifically NEGATION IN A GUARD. Measured, same shape each time:

    union + annotated head + a non-negation guard   -> works
    union + annotated head + negation in the BODY   -> works
    union + annotated head + negation in the GUARD  -> abort

The body works because fz-5xp.38 rewrites `-x` to `Kernel.negate/1`, whose
typed clauses dispatch. A guard is lowered inside the dispatch plan rather than
as a call, so it never reaches that rewrite -- the one place negation still read
a single lane.

FIXED by giving `lower_neg` a runtime-checked branch for the case where neither
lane is provable: test the tag, negate in that lane, box the result. The proven
lanes keep their single instruction.

Pinned by behavior/negate_guard, which covers both branches over floats and
integers plus a union operand no door can decide statically.

WORTH REVISITING: the narrowing itself. A `x :: float` clause head has already
proven the operand's lane by the time its guard runs, so the runtime check is
redundant work the dispatch plan could eliminate. That is a real optimisation
with a real invariant behind it, not a cleanup -- filed separately if it shows
up in a golden.
title: [BUG] Guard negation on an unnarrowed operand aborted natively
